tapes.text:
Somewhere at some level knew about it or you wouldn't be here today and Teddy is right Theo is right you wouldn't be sticking around The true dark energies will not stay there can be doubtful energies don't don't get me wrong Because you are human and you're going to test and you're going to test and maybe you have not experienced this, but everyone who has sat with a great master has experienced it. And you may not even admit it to me. And you may feel so unworthy of that moment that you will hide it from yourself. But you know what I'm talking about. that you go around being a pious-faced fool. But it does mean you will continue to search for that spark for the rest of your existence. And in so doing, you're going to find the truth that you can share with your brother. Because those masters will not lie to you, it will be for your growth, and they'll tease you and they'll test you.

And at some point, you grow enough and that's where you are, Dave. You're too far out here on God's side to go back. And everything else in life is acceptable and it's alright and you can get interested in it, but it has no merit in your daily existence other than it's necessary to perform. And of course while we are having to perform the mundane, our souls long for that connection that isn't ever even broken. But it looks better because it's like the cow we witnessed, you know, the cow sticking her tongue out there as far as she can to get this piece of grass under that fence. And oh my goodness, if she just finally sticks it out a little further and gets it, oh it's choice. Definitely greener.

But what we long for is that womb, that comfort, that security. And yet the womb itself we know is a silent place. And all we are is existing in that. We have left a place where we are all light and creation and experience and no wonder you are allowed to be what I would as nearly as anything call sleep total sleep anesthesia absolutely nothingness except just being you are molding you are making you are becoming and then when you are brought out when you are birthed out of that. It is not like birthing a child into a harsh world. The world may be harsh, but it is like the explosion of the Big Bang. And you won't ever go back from it. And if there is any comfort that I can offer you who search and find yourself falling short of your own expectations of healing, of doing whatever. Well, if I really feel this way, why can I not just heal? Why can I not just lay hands on? Because it's not your business. At the very most, all you There is no job more important than another, only different.

And once you, you don't even have to go through this experience, you just grow into it. EJ would say, well, I just, you know, I have never had anything like that. But by God, we're going to sit with this. I'm going to get it done. Blah, blah, blah, blah. Why? Why? Why does it mean anything to you? Why do you want to go through all this misery? Well, because of my job. And I just will do it. You don't even know why. And then, and then when you sit down and confront yourself, you do know why.

Because this is it. You are realization in a world of total non-realization. Where you're called the insane one. And pretty soon you think, am I? Well, okay, it ain't so bad. If that's sanity, I prefer my way. And at some level I know, at some level, at some level, you wouldn't you can create a different path. And you will. But for those of you fortunate enough to have experienced that moment of, I'm calling it, rebirth. It's not born-again Christianity, it isn't even born-again.

the birthing of soul, who is finally on this side of realization. And where are you going to get this except a teacher is willing to share with you, and you willing to hear? And there is no teacher in the world who is going to waste his time, at least his second time, trying to reach someone who doesn't give a damn. He may try two or three times because of the responsibility he feels, and if he is not heard, he will release you and you will go your way. And some will run from master to master for different reasons. Bogleith runs from thing to thing to thing, hoping to salve his soul from that which he has been. And we look for the perfect religion, the perfect expression.

You're not going to find it there. of the brother who simply has traveled further and you will recognize it and then you're a little embarrassed that it's so so humble and so simple and then you're relieved that you can come in your dungarees and sneakers and be just as at home as if you had dressed up in your tuxedo to go to the award ceremony. Because this is the acceptability of true brotherhood without judgment. That's what you're looking for. And it's so hard to equate when you find it. You just know you're in it. And nothing really is required of you except respect. If you go to visit anyone, Baba is going to insist upon respect, not necessarily for himself, other than he has achieved as the teacher, and would expect you, if you have sought his intelligence, to respect him, to revere him, and if you do not find him to your needs, please leave. And why would you go out and denounce him? Because he differs from your opinion.

And a master will be one who grows great enough to not give a damn about your opinion. He knows he's right. And we as teachers to give in to the silliness of these opinions. Well you know Hatton you're not too bad if you would just. Well fine. If I didn't just would you mind leaving and going and teaching your class somewhere else? Because I am NOT here necessarily as a teacher I'm here to bring you the truth and do my job. If you want great sermons, go down to the Crystal Cathedral or go to the Pope. I am not a preacher, I just sound like one, because I am passionate about what I know. Please, not what I think, what I know. I may have to think about some of the things around here, and that's my opinion. But about God, I know.

I know. And some of you are coming into your knowingness, and it's just about too emotionally strong tenderness to not just bury you in it. And if there is something wrong with wanting to be within God all the time, then man, there's something sick and wrong with me. But you see, I find I can be within God all the time. I am a teacher. Because I care more for my student and the truth of my subject than I care for anything about myself. Anything.

And we have a job to do. We have to walk it together. I don't want to walk it alone. And you're not quite ready. And you better damn well believe I can carry you if I have to. Because there's not a one of you in here that I wouldn't crawl if I had to to carry you. Because you're going to make it. You've already made it. You have already made it. So in your experience, relax and enjoy it. Hold those memories dear.

Because we still have a way to go. And don't stop being lonely for God. Because the minute you stop being lonely for God, you turn to the things of this earth. And they become the big issue. And yet as long as you are of the earth, manifest on the earth with an earthly job, you've got to experience in it and know it. Know it. You can't get by without the things of the world if you're going to be in the world. That's why the everlasting ones will be on the mountaintop. They don't have to be in the world. They will come down to experience in the world if they're needed or if they want to. Just like we have. I didn't say me, This is a game.

This is why we'll win. If you can call it winning or losing, it's only a game. We've already won. And the ones who do not wish to enter this next game we're starting better get off. Because we're going to go right on. And you better well believe, and when you ask, what can you do? Let's create this thing. You've got the tool, let's make it happen. We need the abundance, let's accept it. Let's create it, let's make it happen.

You have the tool, let's precipitate it. Allow it, take it. For goodness sakes, you deserve it. I'm so sick of people thinking they are unworthy. In fact, maybe you deserve more than is thrust off on you. And you humbly think you're not worthy. Oh yes, you are. God does not make errors. Never. It's late and now you've got me all emotionally stirred up. I'm gonna have to go for somebody that their first time here I want to say what an honor it is to be here.

It's been an excellent trip and it's exceeded my expectations beyond anything that I've come to believe that I think that's the way God works is anything that exceeds expectations. Thank you very much. I accept that for everybody here. We are humbled that you would come. And we appreciate it. And we appreciate your words of recognition. Because we are just small. But it's enough. We've got plenty around.

And we're lonely for each other and if you have felt an acceptance here that's all we need that's all we want and we thank you for that is there anything else anyone would like to ask or it has been an amazing few days. Will you help me with my long drive in? He helps me with my long drive out. Ask God. This is what you call the local cop-out. Use your wisdom. If you get tired, rest. There is nothing on the other end that you've got to get there so fast that you risk one moment of infirmity because you were careless.

Not unless you want to learn a hard lesson. And remember something. We need this team. And cutting out on Saturday for any reason is only going to bring you back on Tuesday because we need you. And if there is a relocation, that's acceptable. On the other hand, if you do it out of deliberate carelessness, you're going to have to work anyway and the leg's going to hurt or the back's going to hurt or whatever. Just remember it when you get careless. And if you're ready to go on with our mission, our task, then you'll just put that light around you and you'll say, well, don't go anywhere without that light.

It will shield you from everything. And if you're going to drive, I suggest you get it completely around your vehicle. And you would be amazed if you put it around your vehicle, and I have witnessed it and so have some of you, where a car will go so far over the edge of a cliff that it will just be balanced there. Or it will stop three inches from the barrier, in the cement barrier or the tree. Ask God and God will protect you, but you have to ask. So make it a habit to always ask for protection, but guess what? So you may serve His will. That is not worship, that is respect for your Creator who knows better than you about you and is you.

So everyone, please go in peace, stay in peace, whatever you're going to do, here or there. And one of these days, it is my promise, all of you who would like to be here, will be able to be here. Of course, I may be somewhere else, but I'm going to be here to watch my children grow. We're going to do it. You are going to do it. It It is the demand, the creative ability that will make it work. And if everybody worked at this tonight, for instance, there may be some response tomorrow. But let God find that place, because you don't know where it is. And when you get over the fact that you have to have it according to your limitations and your restrictions, yes, you have to have guidelines, yes, you have to have affirmations, but don't limit them. Because God knows the perfect one. And you don't.

tapes.text:
This is August the 20th, 1996. We decided it just literally on the spur of the moment, so it's made it an incredibly busy morning from daylight on. I had to write a little this morning. We have business that has to be taken care of along with the plans we make otherwise. I realize that we probably should have done this on the last day or so, but it would not have been with good wisdom that we would do it, and I would ask for wisdom in how we handle it today. I have cleared a space so that we won't have any real interference. The most that we may have is an attempt or two to break the shield. So just don't be nervous from any earthquakes or anything that may happen.

I've also cleared it with Edwards to keep clear. It isn't that there is anything at all particularly special, especially to you ones who are local. So, whatever we do the rest of the day, as far as touring or anything like that, people, you don't need to go if you don't want to. There's no point in it. But especially for you ones that are still here, I would like to be able to share before you go, and the reason that I want to tape it pretty carefully is so that we can share with the ones who have been here and already gone home.

The more focused appreciation and energy we can show, the more apt we are to begin to be able to accumulate our abundance. of what it is we are about. We have less interference because what we plan to do is a contribution to everyone, not just to this little handful. Now it can be stated all over the world that the Eckers take the money and run. Well number one, they haven't run far, so they must not have much money. But that's all beside the point. We are outgrowing this sort of quibbling. And we're doing it now. We are getting excellent response.

I'm not, I will just say Africa. Let's just leave it Africa. They're not laughing. They're trying to figure a way to get this done. The obvious thing is that if any nation does it, any central bank does it, it's going to have to mean that there is almost an entirely, a cut rift for the United States of America. And there are plenty of countries who would like to do that, but not the Federal Reserve reserve banks of those countries, which will be called the central banks. And words already gone out and spread out to the banking contacts that you're not to do this or else. Well, some of them aren't going to accept or else.

So the obvious thing is that we will have to get the big hardball players in on it anyway. I don't want to give away strategy. I don't want to talk who. I just want a central focus on getting this done. And that means we don't go ask for a zillion dollars, or I would rather you ask for a zillion dollars in a specific amount. get these things finalized. We were given a limit, a time of response for more information on Monday. Poor Rick's been up since four, taking phone calls from Africa, and I'm telling you we're getting a very decent reception. This is not laughable anymore. And what you don't know is that the politicians of the Republican side, because grandma had already given Clinton several opportunities, so we've not bothered to do much with that administration. I don't think you want a person of that caliber even beginning to represent you. So there is a possibility of being able to do some work with Kemp. When we were working with Donahue, Donahue was a very close personal friend of Kemp's and did have several meetings with him, at which time we were working on cement and housing and low-cost aerated cement housing and modular homes and things like this. And Kemp actually was backing one of those projects and it went south with all of the other problems that we've had had in the Institute.

We can't have these lawsuits all over amongst these attorneys without it taking such an incredible amount of time that we don't have time to get other things done. It isn't that we don't have competent legal help, and especially now, but you keep bringing in attorneys that have to be brought up to speed and everything has to be run past the Eckers. Well, everything has to be run past the Eckers and we may as well not make games out of it. EJ has to make it work some way and therefore, nobody wants to go out and volunteer him to do more or a commander to do more, and everybody says, oh, well, we better check with commander. Well, who's that really mean has to have a meeting? So I'm just trying to explain this morning that nobody is complaining, but it's time for us to focus on some of these other things, the having, the receiving.

What in the hell are we about? about how can we sit here and have a tea party? And I should interrupt and say that over here, Pierre has brought some French cheeses and breads and we wanted to have an opportunity to share that before everybody left. And I didn't want even to specifically call a meeting today because I didn't want anybody to change plans already underway. But we need to look at what we plan to do. And others also were working with us and they understood our plans fairly well until it got to be them and us.

I don't mind them and us, but when I do say, if you do it that way, you will be in competition with us at some point. That is only fair. And if we can't do it anyway, because I am not going to have some damn commune. We have necessities to be done, and every one of the projects could be considered research and development. And yes, we could have gone right to the government and asked for grants. But we don't want to do business like everybody else has done business. It is a lousy way upon which to base an economy. There are some extremely important different items that we need to build here. And yet you can look at your maps, and I want you to look closely at your maps, because regardless of whether or not anything happens, we have to look at all contingency possibilities. At which point you look at Scallion's map, and that's the pretty general picture of the ones who quote are the seers. That you're going to be an island and you will take in probably the Breckenridge line of mountains over here along the Kern River and the Kern River. All of that area will be thrust up for one thing. Then you will have an influx of the ocean property and you may very well lose all of Bakersfield.

This will extend on up beyond Stockton, the island itself. Now that's assuming Scallion is correct. But it will take out your major city or parts of it. It certainly will take out your source of supply, which is L.A. and parts west. You know, anymore, with all the trucking and the shipping and so forth, you will find San Joaquin Valley fruit being sold in New York while you import from Florida. It's a turn into a business. But it's easy enough to divert fruit, for instance, although your lower areas, your more moderate areas for citrus growing may well be gone. That means you're going to have to pretty soon start some kind of citrus operation where you can get it sheltered enough, to warm it enough, to keep some manner of growing capability.

And if we can work quickly enough, and I don't want to put this in your pipe to have smoke dreams or to start planning on it, we can encapsulate or bubble some of the growing fields already there to maintain a transition point for things like citrus fruits that you're going to have to have. And there's some up in the foothills that are touch and go for frost already, but we may be able to salvage some of them and get them sheltered enough before frost or freeze to protect the crops. But we're not going to deal with those concerns now. Those are things that we can do physically after the fact or just at the time of the fact. And you working on them is going to get us closed down. So be reasonable about what you want to do, because if you start out there in an open factory building wireless boxes for total energy consumption, they're going to close you down.

Know it. You've got to have other excuses for doing everything you do from now on in. So you will have what we will call factories of front operation. And it is actually that you will be developing whatever you are doing. But experimentation can be done in those same buildings, even with R&D contracts. We must bring all of our major funding in as R&D or whatever kind of loans we decide to call them. It will be venture capital, but out of our apportionment we will buy our money up front so there is no stock. Not as you think of stockholders out to get all the profits in the world, nor will we accept major interest payments. Pay them double. Therefore we have to have enough funding to be able to do that.

Let us say we borrow from XYZ. Mr. Liebenberg, let's just say we do a joint venture with Liebenberg and he loans us money. He loans us a billion dollars. We will borrow two and give him back one. Right off the top and we're through. You have made money, Mr. Liebenberg. And then at some point, or maybe you pay him back time and a half, so that he makes enough profit to make it worth his while. Or he runs into a trading program where they can make money for him with his money. I'm not trying to change the world.

I'm trying to change this place. But not the place, just what we do. We're not interested in going out and trying to put anybody out of business. But my intent is to have enough to buy the town if we want it. And then you don't have nearly as much trouble with the planning commission, do you? And in the processing, we need enough to be able to put in a proper sewer system with, for instance, a kiln dryer to reclaim that sewage for the fields. And I'm not talking about as fertilizer. I'm talking about as soil. If you have kilns, you can cook that, bake that, and it becomes soil again.

And it is already an operation that is done by others. So we're not talking new. But you have to decide where, and you have to decide how, and you have to do it all within every regulation that comes along. The one thing that may trouble a lot of people, well, I've been waiting around here to run something for 8 years, 10 years. I've been part of this for 150 years and I know that I need to do this. Please don't ask to run that kiln factory if you don't even know what I'm talking about. We will also be able to afford to pull in the expertise. There are zillions of qualified people out of work who know how to do it. Only one qualification. They have to come in and work according to our plan. And just because they're president of the company doesn't mean crap. We want workers.

We want participation. Nobody sitting in their white shirt with their feet on the desk telling the clerk to hide something. And yet we're going to have to structure things according to the modus operandi already established or they will then come in and shut us down. But it will be harder if we own the town. And I'm not talking about running out there with our placards and becoming sovereign. I'm talking about owning the town. And then we work just exactly as we have, but you can see we need a lot. And I want your energy poured toward getting these things finalized, we've got enough established. Trust me, we have enough, just our portion established, to do three or four or five of these pods. And they will be totally done within the workings of what is already established.

We are going to need Costco type warehouses. We want to build a factory outlet. We are going to have a complex. We'll show you where. That will outdo anything around, and we will want to build a type of resort area with it where people want to come out here just to shop, and there will be a nice parking place where you can camp for the weekend, and we can also have what we will call a closed gated operation like at Costco so that you can keep tabs over who is here and who is expected. And if we have a major, major upheaval, the people who are members will have a place to come and park their recreational vehicle. We can close the gates and keep all of that food storage and clothing storage and furniture storage that is within that, quote, compound. I don't know what else to call it that you will understand, and I don't want to make big explanations for this tape that I hear about in a Nevada court. I want this to be taken seriously. No more footsie playing. This is serious time. It's happening. It's coming down. And I want you to be a part of it. I don't want you to be on the outside wondering What the hell you're missing?

And if we can't do it that way, then we don't deserve to be able to do it at all. This is not child play. This is adult, mature growth and building, and doing it within a society where we meet every law, every regulation, and we don't have to hide anything. And that is what, quite frankly, has done us in good stead all the way. And the adversary and the people that have stood against us are going to fall. I'm sorry. I don't know any other way to put it. They're going to fall. Because they have done it to themselves.

We have not lied. We are touted as being a bunch of liars and an asshole in these things. We have not lied. Every story coming back is filled to overflow with total obscene lies and ridiculous things. And I'm going to have trouble today with her voice. I do this, I yell, and then I pay. I don't have a speaker, you know, after an hour. But I'm passionate about this. This is our mission. This is our mission. And you've heard it now for three days. Our mission is God in a survival of a remnant.

I don't know how to make you understand. I just hope you will accept and pray that it doesn't happen too soon. It is going to happen. Things are already so off balance that many of these things cannot be stopped, why would you stop the evolution of a globe, a planet? To retain the dark forces in a city like L.A.? Am I saying that I want to topple off L.A. and kill all those people? No. But you must be prepared, mustn't you, if you survive. We cannot change some of the things that will happen, but we can change our own environment. And yes, we can do it.

And you will have other ruins found throughout this world where obviously they were eating dinner and something happened. Some happened like Pompeii and you see the bodies. Things have happened like the Mayans and you don't see anything except supper on the table. That's because they were taken up. And it wasn't because they were such damn good people. They sacrificed people. For goodness sakes, evil has always reached a point, an epitome. And many were taken up and fled the place and went to places like Orion. And maybe that's why Sirius and Orion is the middle of the buffalo and Sirius is the tail. Don't worry about it. Keep your connection with God and you'll end up on the nose and that's the best place to be.

Or ride between God's horns, because he's going to have a craft on either tip to look after you. I want today to share with you. That means we're going to have to split up and look intelligent. We're not going to go rent buses or anything. And some of you local ones may not want to bother to make the trip. We can do that another day. But the ones who are out of town obviously aren't going to have another opportunity. So I felt that maybe if we could agree and handle this properly and make no big issue of it so that the cup went out today, we would like to caravan around and show you.

I will make a running tape and ask others to have input so that by the time we're done with the trip, you will all have everything that takes place. And we will begin over, well, we'll be, well, never mind, we will begin. I felt that if we met here first, we would give any late comers, like us, an opportunity to get here. And I don't know who all might come. It isn't important because if they are out of town here, they have another opportunity and maybe they've already seen part of this. So I have to just let you decide how you want to handle it, we'll drive along in a caravan and we will look at these places. And then I want it very carefully considered. There are some places that I would like to take you that are right on the beaten path, Right on everybody basically has been there, but they don't know anything about what they're about.

And these things I don't want chitter-chattered about. I don't want to compete for to-cuntulous land. Anybody who has land and anything that will be purchased here will be fair market value. They'll be overpaid for their land. And a lot of them are expecting this so they are really hiking that price. But I want you to understand something. During this period of time where some others held land, what I considered, and I told them at the time, I really do appreciate you guys holding this land. What I do not appreciate, gentlemen, is that you have held this land, and you have all but lost it, and it's gone into foreclosure, but you want to charge us back our own development improvements.

That's a no-no. I won't accept that. And people will say, well, why hasn't it built up more? Well, why in the world would it build up more when your major industry here is a prison, an aerospace bedroom, and they've laid off thousands of aerospace people? We're going to build on North Ahatchapee. I don't give a damn what they call it. They call it Capitol Hills. I really appreciate what these people did. And we've met with them and we have, we helped lay out this. And Capitol Hills over here, North Tehachapi, and we will go back to calling it North Tehachapi.

I don't like Capitol Hills. I don't like the term Technopolis. Can we use Tehachapi North? Tehachapi North is wonderful. We're going to build motion picture studios, network television, we're going to run cables through there, we're going to have domes, some of them 30 stories high. And it is already laid out on the pattern of Atlantis. It's going to have circular drives, pods of domes, industry. It's going to have a P Soup Anderson type of restaurant motel. We've already worked with it.

Those people have been out years ago to set it up. It will have a truck stop and a soup kitchen and a place where truckers can pull off, have a bath, have a warm supper, and enjoy our place. We are going to have this resort area near our Costco complex, and I'm calling it that because we're getting the head of Costco development to do it. He's been waiting for five years for us to get our shit together. We're going to bring some Anderson's Steak Houses out here. We've been busy. And every time we have one more adversarial attack, I get so pissed off I can't stand it. And I'm not one you want to have pissed off at you. Today is a change. This weekend, you got your message. It's a spiritual journey. It is flat, out of time, time. And I'm going to push forward and I'm going to get this done. And I don't give a damn what those others want out of us. You can spread the word, Ms. Tootin, Mr. Fort is going to get the money from Dave Overton.

That is blasphemy. And neither is Horton and Abbott, who have taken advantage of these people to the point taken their money to lie to the court. It isn't going to happen. Now those people can start working with us, or they can stay on the outside, I don't give a damn which. But the lying, the cheating, and the thieving is going to stop. Now Mr. Ince thinks that these people are packed, and they have their suitcases under the crawlspace, and that one is an affidavit to court. Now, how the hell would he know?

And if they were, they wouldn't put it under the floor, they'd put it in the attic, wouldn't they, Charles? Those kinds of games are for kindergarten. I understand they have what they consider an investment. It was not an investment, it was loans. They understood exactly what they were doing when they did it. I'm getting on with it. I just want it clearly understood what we're about before we walk out that door. Because I am going to show you what we plan to do and where we plan to do it. And I have to trust you, don't I?

Because I'm going to share some spiritual things with you that will blow your minds. And after today, all of we local ones can go up there and experience this. So it is mainly important that our guests be able to go and experience. You're going to have to consider Scallion's map over here, and here's I guess another one that will allow you to have some idea about what you may look like. life. You will be the larger island in this chain. Now here is a topographical map that is just interesting. I don't see any reason to make a big deal of it. Here is Bakersfield. You can see that it is in the lower lands. And if you have water moving in through here, it's going to get those oil fields. But I also want to tell you that politically, satanically, Bakersfield is the darkest spot west of the Mississippi. So hold it in your heart. Moving on down here, here is Bear Mountain, which you will see, which can be pointed out outside here.

It's over here. And then Tehachapi is nestled in here. Above 4,000 feet, you can expect a 1,200-foot rise of portions like Tehachapi. We have cradled the whole of the crystal, six miles around that crystal, so that we can lift it out so that it doesn't fracture the crystal. Don't concern yourself with it. We think that we have it pretty well stabilized that a 3.7 quake is the highest that will hit this area as a magnitude. So it'd be a natural quake. Obviously, if you're going to be shoved up, there will be disruption, but I believe that we can hold it to the 26-mile diameter of not too much incredible damage.

I can't promise it because of the White Wolf Fault underneath this place. Took out this entire town in the early 50s. But we have relieved pressure off of it. We have had now out near Sweet Ridge and Mojave, we have experienced quakes of four and five magnitude and nobody in Tachipee knew it. So we've had an opportunity to run some tests. As you move in the other areas, I think it's 99, I'm not sure, Gorman, that area anyway, that is a trigger point. When it goes along the Gorlock Fault over there, it's going to trigger the San Andreas at the LA area.

The trigger point is not out here. But of course you cannot control what happens along the full distance of the fault. But enough strain has been relieved that it'll probably, you know, I think it'll just kind of bypass you. And the San Andreas and the Garlock will do a lot of damage probably also in Bakersfield. And we cannot expect to be anywhere on this continent and not expect some damage. But I was a little relieved just before this weekend for eight years, Dharma has had bungees around everything in the house. And she said, oh what the hell, the rubber bands are breaking I just may as well leave them off. And so she said, Dad, you said 3.7 it's up to you. And I heaved a sigh of relief because if we have to attend every quiver as if it's our last, nobody can focus on what we need to do, especially her. And I really am leaving more and more and more of that kind of information, unfortunately, for the ones having to receive it, but for SolTech.

It doesn't mean that you can't or shouldn't watch it and take care. For goodness sakes, take care of yourself as if you're going to have a 9-point earthquake and a 3.7 is going to make you smile. We have so many earthquakes around here, so many blasts against our shield. We'll do a little bit of dialogue here, monologue I guess. We're now traveling toward Water Canyon. We come up Bacchus Road, turned east on High Line, and we're just about to turn up Water Canyon. This is going to be a little bit awkward for all you listeners. I don't know how we're going to shift this microphone back and forth, and I don't know how to get her eyes open along with her mouth.

So we're going to have to move along here, feeling our way. We're headed up Water Canyon, which becomes an extremely, extremely important location. And I would like to speak loud enough for the ones in the rear to hear, but I'm going to lose her voice if I shout. As we get to the top of this place, we're going to, there will be a Y in the road, and we will take the one to the left and move up to the county park just to drive through it so that ones can understand the difference in the vegetation as we come up this canyon. As we get to the area of the park, you'll find that there are some very large evergreens, and it will almost be like moving into a different land, if you will, as we move into a higher altitude. You'll have this same repetition across the road as we get to the broom property this afternoon.

We will not be able to go onto the broom property because it has been kept in its rather... Oh, go! Oh, I think you got him. We just, we'll have a lot of interruptions along the way and a lot of clicks and clacks because we're having a little trouble with buttons and things. At the top of this park, it moves on to some higher country. There are your hawks, don't miss them. They're always up here. This is grandfather's land. We'll have to look very carefully. Yes, it's the golden eagle. It's a juvenile. Do you want to stop here and take a picture or do you want to wait until you come back? This is a very, very important place for the big birds. We have the eagles up here, and this is the place where we have released some of the condors to reintroduce into the wild.

But what we have here always are the golden eagles, and we have the imperial eagles, a pair, that have now nested, so there are more than one, and these we call the Phoenix. These are the ones that are the imperial eagle of the Philippines, called the Philippine bird, but it is the Phoenix, and it was missing for many, many, many years. This is a blessing. These were brought here because of our people here, and with any kind of luck, maybe they will be sighted today. But we just passed some golden eagles and some red tails. We are entering the park now. This is a holy place. They didn't know it when they built the park here. message here for Little Crow some years ago, an altar, and he got his message and it's a very wonderful place to be. I'm going to just sign off until we come up to a place where we can stop at the top of this. I just want everybody to be able to visualize we're now in the very tall pines, very beautiful up here.

E.J., you will please pause as we go past the place where the altar on a little lower level. And I will explain the altar itself. It was a pottery container, crow feathers because of little crow, bits and pieces. Now this is called Carl's Rock and you will have noticed that there is a sign there that says Carl's Rock. Not to be confused, it's not Little Crow's. Little Crow's name before Carl Bryant died and went his way was Little Crow.

tapes.title: Valley Of Radiance, Sacred Ground
tapes.excerpt: We don't need to pause too long and everybody can have a copy of these tapes later. tapes.text:
We don't need to pause too long and everybody can have a copy of these tapes later. The reason that this is so extremely important is in cases of emergency necessity for living facilities, you can bring tents up here to the right, it circles on around the hillside. And that is private ground. And you will not be usually allowed beyond this point. But there are some buildings up there that are for special problem children, usually use it in the summer. And so there are some barracks rooms and then if you look around you can see that there is a lot of wooded area and all the way to the top it's going to become mandatory that we have this land and you will see it again from the other side as we go up toward what is the YMCA camp this will be a very easy area to defend and let me tell you why I have to speak of defense if and when you are quote invaded from below you're going to need to head up one of these canyons so that we can protect it by cutting it off at the bottom you can see as you came up here that it will be easy to block the road now i'm not talking about bringing your machine guns up here, I'm talking about coming up here for security.

And you're going to have to understand that I am your security. We're not going to start a war. You're going to find that major facilities across this mountain, extremely important ones, Northrup, and that has an entire tunnel system that hooks into Edwards. I have an extremely good working relationship with those people. There are already aliens completely outfitted under the ground living in those tunnels and living in those cities. And a lot of the people who live in Tehachapi actually live and work underground over there across the mountain. They are absolutely sworn to secrecy on the advent of their death, or death of their family, if they tell what they do. So when you have somebody who says, I work in the aerospace industry, do them a favor, don't ask what they do. Don't put them on the spot to either lie or shift or fudge. Those are not our aliens over there, they are fabrications, but I'm going to say something that I rarely say outside the room.

And that is that they are absolute, total crossbreeds robots. There are some very lizard-looking people and every now and then they are trained by bringing them out and they have many times, many times been seen over in Stallion Springs and Bear Valley and outlying places, they rarely are ever allowed to get as far down as the city itself. But over at, for instance, on Adam Drive on Eckers Place, we will just call it Eckers Place even though we're having a lot of dispute over it, they will come down that far. But that is mainly because the military keeps the place under such close surveillance. Always if these guys get loose, they are very very curious, they are very very docile. And the only frightening thing about them is their appearance. They will have slit eyes.

Usually. Not all of the genetic structure is picked up to produce slit eyes. But they are trained to be able to see through slit eyes at night. They are genuinely nice beings, but if they come upon your car, they will turn everything on. They will try. They won't try to drive it. They are curious. They will go through everything that you've got, and they will push every button. You'll have your wipers going, and your ashtray out and everything will be working. They are not brilliant. They're not trained to be brilliant. They are trained to be trained and scare the daylights out of everybody they encounter. Very often they will come out of the facility and they'll over across the way into the flat toward Lancaster and Mojave area.

They will come out and they'll climb up on the rooftops and things like that. So very shortly after they appear will also appear the military brigade. So don't sweat if you run into one. Roby had an experience with a couple who came to call when he was building up on the mountain. But that's why this is so important. I have my own agreements made. There will be no air traffic of danger, dangerous variety coming over any part of these ridges. So if in fact you needed to retreat to this hilltop, you would be safe. Because you all know that all they've got to do is bring a helicopter over. And we may very well be visited by a few of those black ones before we get through today, but I don't think so.

I think they'll just pull back everything. This is our day. And I do have agreements. And it's not too wise to cross me too often. So shall we move on? Yes, next stop. We have to be extremely careful because this property belongs to private parties and we certainly don't want to become unpopular with them while we're dickering to purchase it. You'll notice there are three dwellings, very elderly dwellings down here. There is one of at least three.

Stop before you intersect and we'll pass you there. Just go right over there and stop. I would point out that there are dwellings here, very close. This is one of three or four little lakes. Very good water supply up here. On up the road that we're traveling, off to the left, there is a beautiful spring, but we also have people out here working the land, and we don't want to disturb or cause any problem with the people who live here. Off to the left, maybe a mile, is a wonderful spring. You will be able to see a massive rock up here as we go along. On up this road is a YMCA camp called Earl Anna.

We have diggered with them about buying this entire mountainside and all of that camp. And it's in limbo land. People will notice in this vehicle that you will have the bluebirds flying back and forth across the road. We had the juvenile eagles up in sight, but they have now turned their attention to the man watering, so we may not get to see them again. I'm sorry we didn't stop. We can't have time to go all the way up to the camp, building, a large kind of center building, and we will stop here. As the stream comes down, its headwaters are up at the camp area, and that's one reason that it's so important to have the camp area. This is an area where the stream comes down, and there is a little place here called the weir, where on certain days, water is diverted or else it's left open to run freely into a little lake to the right and a little lake to the left on down the hill. This is one of the most important places in this entire area and this is where I have to ask your indulgence to be to be cautious about how you handle yourself. This is very, very sacred ground up here.

This is Tecantla's place. I have really pondered whether or not I could bring you. I believe that it is worthy enough for us to stop and be able to experience this. I'm not going to give any more location about any more coordinates. I don't want everybody just running up here, but it is the place where the Indians will come up to the Indian campground This has just been a meeting of the elders of the various tribes up at that campground this weekend And this is the place they climb the fence and come over to So I'm going to share that with you And I'm just going to have to trust that everybody will be worthy of their word and keep quiet about it let's please let's please you are in god's temple here you don't have any idea on what sacred ground you stand and we will have reverence i had just put on the tape that i have to ask your indulgence and your absolute reverence to this place.

This is it. I'm not going to give the coordinates. I would like for you to look around. I would like for you to look at the hair on your arm as we move toward these places. We're going to cross the stream. You're going to get goose pimples. I repeat, this is T'Konchala's land, this is for Little Crow, and there are things deep in the heart of this place underneath us that would blow your mind. And I don't want to say much more about it, let us quietly go and let us experience, because this is it.

This is why we are here. It's not the crystal, but this is sacred. This is what would be called the Awakan Wakon, the holy altar. The bluebirds nest up here and usually they come to feed their young at this little stream. It's a little late. Carry a cross? No, no, I don't need that. I've got my pack of these.

As you come up to this area, you will realize that this is not a natural formation, although it's forever been here. I'm not going to explain what that is, but we will come down here and then I want you just to quietly experience for a moment Marina is Indian she understood it immediately and I wish all of you could share that this is what we call the heart of the mother, right here. On the first journey up here for these ones, grandfather spoke and said, get little crow up here, this is his land. And it doesn't matter how many times this land changes hands.

This will be the mother, the altar. This is where the heartbeat is. This is where the ancient things are that will bring you back to knowledge. It's a sacred place. Some of these little stops have to be very short because we have ones who need to catch a plane in LA to go back to Hawaii. So we're just going to kind of skim over the rest of everything. This was the most important part to experience. The rest can even be handled from the vehicles if we need to. I would have spoken about and let them take pictures of what we call the acorn woodpeckers up here, who actually destroy some of the trees.

But, unfortunately, it also becomes a landmark for the local people, and we don't want people just running up here. I want to comment a little bit along the way. As we travel down this road, we're going to have to cut quite a bit of this little trip short because, as I said before, we have ones that must catch a plane in L.A. That means we've got to wrap up in these hinterlands so that they can be on the right road when they need to go. As we come along this valley road, you'll notice a lot of orchards. It became so incredibly expensive to irrigate that most of the older orchards that were actually prize-winning orchards have been removed.

This was all orchard land. I'm speaking to the ones in the car. This was called Nears Orchard. And we were unable to get control of it before they had to close it. We just did not have the resources. This is really sad because you're going to live on fruit. And if we were to go farther up there, up this road, we're going to turn left so that we can see other more important land points. But there is an entire area very close to Tehachapi downtown that is called Noon's Ranch. And we have been negotiating with that and they held it for us for three years, but we just couldn't do it.

So most of those prime apple orchards have been removed off of it, but it is extremely prime growing land. And in fact, there has been several attempts to break that land up into housing developments. It's extremely important that not happen because on the Nunes property, they also have the prime wells in the area, and they trade off water out of the aqueduct, et cetera, for irrigation for the wonderful water that comes out of the ground to feed the city of Tehachapi. And anyone looking at this as we come down out of the foothills will see that we are looking across the way to the other side of this valley, the Tehachapi Valley. Remembering that Tehachapi itself means land of plenty acorns, winds, clear winds, clean winds, clear water, and abundance.

It is the valley of radiance, Tejas Chape, which all you Texans will understand Tejas, you would spell it Texas, T-E-X-A-S, if you were down in Texas. And from that has come the term Tehachapi, which is an Indian name, but it is recognized by us as Tehachapi. As we go directly across the valley, we can look at the area as we go by and make a turn onto the freeway because we want to go down as far as at least the Broom Ranch off-ramp toward Keene. And we'll need to gather to speak just a little bit, but we better keep our speaking to an absolute minimum. And people traveling along even with us are just going to have to get a set of tapes, go or get them later because I don't believe that we have time to stop and have a little lecture every place and I can be talking along the way. There is a lot of land still left in Tachepee.

Very low development so far. As you look across the way, the water treatment plant or the sewer plant is off here for the area of Golden Hills, etc. But it certainly will not be able to handle what will be the influx as building happens, There is a prime railroad leg that runs through here and one reason that we need to make this route is that I want to be able to show, to have a picture in your mind why this area is so extremely important. You see, you're going to have a major break at the San Andreas Fault. It's going to be almost impossible to come by land from the sea area. As you head out toward the southern direction, you're going to find that you run into the Mojave Desert, but you will also probably be cut off at the Garlock Fault.

So most of the influx will be needing to come in through Bakersfield to the north. And up here between us and Bakersfield, along about the Broom Ranch, or the way station as we call it around here, there is a highway way station where the road gets very narrow. There is a back road, but we can easily plug that road with one blast and secure this town. And don't misunderstand what I say by one blast. I'm talking about the hillside, not blasting you with lasers. This is a major truck route, and these truckers need a place to stop. And if and when things begin to break up, they're going to be pulling out of the major city as rapidly as they can if they're on the outskirts and are able to get across the faults at all. You're going to end up with a lot of traffic in this area cut off. So you better hope that those truckers are carrying something you can use. To the right here we have now made a turn on Highway 58 toward Bakersfield and all of this area for 12 miles is what is called the Broom Ranch. It is almost in its pristine state. There are not more than two or three buildings on it at all. The old The fourth branch place is to the left of the freeway and has never been developed.

Mr. Broom bought this as an investment by flying over it. He has never allowed very much development. He runs cows and he has a cattle crew. There is a cinnabar mine that we will pass up here, and it is extremely valuable. It will need some attention in the beginning because it will be near where it could be residential areas. And in that mine will be some mercury so that we will not want all of that toward the surface. There are other elements in it that are absolutely mandatory and I have told these ones before. The broom ranch becomes extremely important because in doing a project proposal there is enough land that is developable to go ahead and lay it out in estate lots. Every time you do a project you must make it in a way that it will sell itself to any investor. And so many estate lots become worth so much money and then these proposals become valid banking instruments.

And it doesn't matter how we're going to get our money, we have to have valid banking instruments. We're not going to do business outside the loop of the way business is done. We just won't do it otherwise. And whether or not this land is ever developed, it will have to show development. So everything to the right of this freeway as we pass here all the way to the little town of Keene is Broom Ranch property. And it goes over a period of three mountain ranges. There are what, 26,000 acres overly?

24,000. 24,000 attached to the Capitol Hills area makes about 31,000 acres that can come under development for our needs. If you go down through Caliente, which we will not do today, and go up then toward Walker Basin, you will pass a little place called Lorraine. And Lorraine is just a little wide place in the road, but it can be reached if the proper roads are built, or you will not even want to have it reachable except through locked gates because your security comes on the backside of this loop ranch. You can get all the way over to this little town of Lorain, and it's very rugged country on the other side. You could maybe raise some cattle.

In between there are some places called Tweedy Creek, which could be utilized a little bit for some agriculture, but most of this land is pretty rugged. And you want to keep it that way. Over on the opposite side, there is another ranch, which I will not name, and it has 14 running springs, year-round springs. So the water has to be considered. That will be your major, major problem. So we must have land that has water, and good water. And it must be protected. We have driven along here, and now I believe for the visitors here in the car, you'll be able to see that the railroad runs here to the left, and it will come down to a hill that we will point out, which is called the loop.

This whole area is also called the loop ranch. Actually a youngster kind of designed this loop. They run such heavy, lengthy trains up through here that they couldn't even with seven or eight booster locomotives pull the hill. So they have taken and tunneled. They run a railroad around the outside, which becomes a loop, and a train will cross over itself because it's tunneled. And if it's coming uphill, especially important, is to make this loop within the hill and encircle the hill, and then you can come out at the proper altitude to make it on into Tehachapi because Tehachapi summit is the highest place in this area.

And that's the way it was chosen to be handled. So railroad buffs come from all over, all over the world to witness this feat of engineering. And it is on the left-hand side of this freeway going toward Bakersfield. Here we can't see very well, but we can see a dig up there for the cinnabar mine, and they've mined it down below there. Hopefully those other folks will catch up. I would, well, Gail is not local but any local people can catch up and literally come down here this afternoon. It doesn't, we just need to make sure that the ones going to Hawaii get out of here on time. We're not going to pause, but just for a minute, I'll try to get everything I can onto this tape.

We want our Hawaiian friends to know that we're going to cut this very, very short. Anyone local can come back out here and look at this. So I want them to be able to see everything at least, and they can get the tapes, and they can catch up. If you go on down this freeway, you will pass the loop, where I have just explained the railroad, just you who are local know about it, it is the central point of discussion always in this place for tourists. The trains come and to get up this hill, even with booster locomotives, they have to go in through the tunnel and then loop around the outside of the hill, and then they're coming out at an altitude where they can make it on into Tehachapi. It also reduces the speed as they come down the hill to go toward Bakersfield.

It's just a point of interest. The thing I wanted them to see is all this property down to the little town of Keene is called Broome, Broome Ranch, B-R-O-O-M-E, as you will see on this off ramp. There is a Cinnabar mine here, right off in this direction. I don't want to discuss it very much because it does contain mercury and we will probably bury most of it. We have had this land in negotiations with Mr. Broom for years. He just wanted 13 million dollars and we didn't have it. They have kept it in a very pristine state. They run cattle. He has his own operatives that run cattle. It basically has not been developed otherwise. Except the only piece of property remaining with this broom property, which is 24,000 acres, is the loop itself. And the little ranch dwellings and things, the old homestead burned, but there are some that's where the bunkhouses and things are for the ones that run.

And anybody who wants to drive out the old road this afternoon and come and watch these trains, it is fascinating. All over the world they come to look at this loop. And it's just because it's interesting. I wanted you to see the land. From here it will extend like three little mountain ranges. That includes this 24,000 acres. On the back side is a place where we must have a way to get through. And there is an old road. When we get to Sand Canyon, you will know that there is an old road that, with lock gates and so forth, that will allow you to go over this range.

But it isn't for public travel. There are ranches on both sides, and it's at the end of Sand Canyon. But that can be upgraded enough to be able to get through to the other side. Now why would you want to get to the other side? Because it has that piece of property that backs this one, and we have investigated it. It was for sale also, but we delayed again. But it has 14 year-round running springs on it. And about all you can do with it. You can run a few cows and there's a pretty good cattle operation, a little town of Lorraine. It's all over this hill.

To get to Lorraine now, you go up on down this road, turn right, and you would go into Caliente, up toward Walker Basin, but if you keep going you will come to this little beautiful wonderful little busy town of Lorraine. Any questions here or can we move right on? I'll try to get it as much as I can while I talk in the car. Since we're not going to be able to take this caravan on one leg of the trip that I had truly wanted to to show them but as EJ Suggested most got to see it from the air directly across from this property is What is called the Keene Ranch? property It's a little more toward Keene, but it runs all the way into the property, actually, behind the Eckers.

And that's one reason it's never been developed. That particular property right at their property line does not belong to the Keene Ranch, but basically it's not developable either. There is a wonderful valley up in there, absolutely marvelous valley up in that area and will be prime place to have a dairy chickens animals out of the way out of sight. It can also be developed and there would be some land in in that little valley that could be is arable but I don't think you would ever want to do more than raise grain and hay for for the dairy itself. But we're not going to do that today. My intent as we go along, and we've not been able to talk about the projects, we didn't even get to the list before we went.

We knew we would be very, very short of time, but we'll cram in as much as we can. You see, part of the reason that I wanted to do this was so that, let us say you are a dairy farmer, or you have always wanted to be a dairy farmer. For instance, in the state of California, as you go up toward Fresno and Sacramento, from here, you will find an area of many, many dairy farms. Most of those are owned and operated by a family called the Jensen's. Now we have access to Cal Jensen who is of that family. His whole life has been in dairy farming as a for instance. But he's not necessarily the only dairy farmer. Some of you are going to know how to raise chickens. We're not interested in raising chickens to kill and eat because we're going to raise soybeans and we're not going to kill off our animals just for the hell of eating beefsteak, for instance.

And when you are having winds at 200 miles an hour sustained, you're going to have to get these animals into shelter. Up at the Keene Ranch that I was just speaking of, it is sheltered, already is sheltered. But you're still going to have to build semi-underground barns. You can either build them entirely underground so that you can use the top of it for growing or above ground use. But these animals are going to have to be protected from the severe winter and the severe heat of summer. You are going to move into almost two seasons, period. Extreme heat, extreme cold. You won't recognize seasons.

There are going to be so many seasonal hot spells and so many seasonal, unseasonal, cold spells that you're going to shake your head. They're already shaking their head. That's part of the reason so many of the apple orchards are gone after hundreds of years of being able to grow things in this valley. Suddenly, they freeze. So already the changes are taking place. And you who are listening and wonder what in the world your talents might be used for, consider these things as we discuss. Everybody is not going to come out here and be an actor in a motion picture studio, but maybe you know how to run a camera. There will be plenty of available people, but we're going to need substantial numbers of people to build from.

And certainly we do want to build with our own crew where we can. So just keep these things in mind as we talk about them. We've got to have everything from grist mills to pencil making facilities. So when you ask, what can I do? I can't answer you what can you do. You're going to have to see what maybe you can do and let us see how it unfolds. And it's going to take a while yet to be able to do that. And we can't sustain any more load here right now. But as you speak with yourself and you speak with God, you're going to know. You don't have to ask us. Please realize that all of this land here and part of this by Mr. Broome's son has applied for and I believe has been approved for some development to work adjacent to the Capitol Hills property.

You can see that that ranch is an incredible piece of property because it runs for 10 to 12 miles, just linearly here along this freeway, which is a major, major circulation route for trucking, and this railroad. We're going to come up here and turn off and move into what is now called the Capitol Hills area. There is only an ARCO station built on that very beautiful piece of valley land. And it has been zoned for development, so we would not have much of a problem with it. The beautiful aspect of this is that the land is still here, the infrastructure that is in for the commercial district is approved, the curved, circular structure of Atlantis. And I'm going to ask that E.J. discuss this when we get up here and point out the various and sundry places and the intended use of this particular property. So I personally will sign off.

Commander asked me to give you a brief description of this particular situation here. We're at Tehachapi North. It's comprised of 2100 acres, 975 acres of which is next to the city of Tehachapi and has been zoned for commercial and residential development. The biggest dome for the inside Futuronics movie studio is assumed to be roughly in the middle of that flat area out there. And around that, we think we'll wind up with at least five other major domes. The center one, the big one, should be 450 feet in diameter and roughly 220 feet tall. That's roughly 20 to 25 stories. Give you an idea of the size of it. So it should be a major development, extremely attractive to people who would want to stop. We could have actually something like a Disneyland here if we wanted to.

I don't think that's the objective, naturally. But anyway, that's in that area and around that are the other domes. That's the center of the city and there are plenty of places for university type things, places for people to come and learn things and then in the foothills lots of areas for lovely home sites. I believe that pretty well does it for me here. Doris is going to give you a talk now. Well, over here to the left, just before you get to what I was just describing in the car as the broom property, and Mr. Broom's son had already been able to annex part of that, where it starts up the hill, that's broom property. But before you get there, as you see when we drive out to the right, is an area there that will be a complete P. Anderson's pea soup thing with its windmill and all that stuff.

And there will be a truck stop and a place for those truckers to have a soup kitchen and facilities. It will be a major motel. We've already had the people out to look at that, and they've already agreed to do it. And then as we move on down toward that end, as we go by, it's simply because...

tapes.excerpt: Now if we're not wiping out tape one. Okay. All right. Landfall gravity. So on down here we will continue to build little pods of these dome things.
